title: Securing Edge AI Workshop
text:
About the Workshop
Connected devices are embedded throughout our homes, cars, factories, and critical infrastructure, yet device security has often taken a backseat to other considerations, such as power management and latency. As the prevalence of edge devices increases, security challenges, such as resource efficient cryptography, securing over-the-air updates, and defending against side-channel attacks, need to be addressed. This workshop aims to inform participants about the risks to edge devices and provide the tools to defend against them.

Workshop Topics

How AI is changing the Cybersecurity Landscape: Are the new tools introducing new threats?
Threat modelling for constrained device: Identify and mitigate security risks at the edge.
Lightweight cryptographic protocols: Secure communications and authentication with minimal overhead.
Secure firmware & OTA updates: Protect device integrity with secure boot and update strategies.
Edge network intrusion detection: Detect anomalies and attacks in resource-constrained networks.

Seán Ó Fithcheallaigh
PhD Researcher, Ulster University.
Seán is a PhD Researcher within the Pervasive Computing Research Centre (PCRC), specialising in Federated Learning (FL) with a focus on developing trustworthy FL frameworks for sensor networks and IoT devices. He is also a researcher with the BT Ireland Innovation Centre (BTIIC), where he works on IoT Autonomics. With over a decade of experience in electronics and software engineering, including developing next-generation application-specific IoT sensors, he brings first-hand understanding of the practical constraints and opportunities that shape AI deployment at the edge.
